title: The quiet moment between repetitions
note: The hard part is drawing nothing happening. Every instinct of an illustration model is to give the pair an activity, and any activity here is the wrong picture: this step exists to show a dog who has been asked for nothing and is fine.
scene: The entry hall, a few steps back from the closed charcoal front door. Nothing is being asked of Lucy and nothing is being offered. She stands on all four feet beside the handler, loose and neutral — weight even, tail down and relaxed, head level, looking off toward the middle distance rather than at the handler, at the door, or at the viewer. She is not sitting. The handler stands beside her, upright and easy, both arms hanging at her sides: not reaching, not gesturing, not in the treat pouch, not looking down at Lucy. She looks quietly ahead. The black leash is clipped to the ring on Lucy's collar, hangs down in a deep slack curve to the floor and lies loose there; the handler holds its loop lightly in one lowered hand. Draw the leash with a thin lighter outline where it passes near her coat so it stays readable, and never across her back or shoulders. Neither of them is engaging the other. Background: the lavender wall, one baseboard line, the closed door and the doormat well off to one side. Plenty of empty floor.
mustBeTrue: nobody is doing anything — the handler's hands are empty and at her sides, she is not looking at Lucy and Lucy is not looking at her, no treat and no cue is being offered — Lucy is standing rather than sitting with a relaxed neutral posture, and the leash hangs in a visibly slack curve rather than a straight or taut line.
